By Raphael McMahon @raffmcmahon Published 10/10/26 AT 1:04 PM EDT Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share on LinkedIn Share on Reddit Share on Flipboard Share on Pocket King Khalid International Airport. GETTY IMAGES King Khalid International Airport, one of the busiest airports in the Middle East, was evacuated on Saturday after the Iran-backed Yemeni group reportedly attacked Terminal 3 of the transportation hub. Sources on the ground in Riyadh heard explosions and claimed that dozens were injured in the attack, with at least five Saudi nationals undergoing intensive care, according to AFP. A diplomatic source told the French international news agency that the attack occurred at 3PM local time (8AM eastern time) on Saturday. "Houthis are attacking civilian targets. Riyadh airport is a civilian target," the source added. At least 12 were killed and over 300 were injured, the New York Times reported . The U.S. embassy in Riyadh said it was "aware" of the attacks and strongly recommended that "all U.S. citizens avoid this airport and surrounding areas." Aviation tracker FlightRadar also shows that all flights to the Saudi capital have either been cancelled or diverted to other destinations.
